findings.reason: parser.ts:1452 only does state.position++. The removed skipByteOrderMark also set lineStart. For '﻿foo: 1\nbar: 2', skipSeparationSpace (1455) doesn't touch lineStart on the first line, so blockIndent = position - lineStart (1243) is 1. The second line has lineIndent 0, which ends the mapping at 1131, and readDocument then throws at 1419-1422.
findings.claim: The leading-BOM skip moves position past the BOM but leaves lineStart at 0. As a result, BOM-prefixed files with more than one top-level key or sequence entry fail to parse.
findings.evidence:
Line 1452 runs `if (state.input.charCodeAt(state.position) === 0xFEFF) state.position++` and does not set `state.lineStart = state.position`. The removed `skipByteOrderMark` did both. Trigger: `load('﻿foo: 1
bar: 2
')`. In parseNode, `blockIndent = state.position - state.lineStart` (line 1243) is 1, so readBlockMapping runs with nodeIndent 1. On the second line `lineIndent` is 0, and `state.lineIndent < nodeIndent` (line 1131) ends the mapping. readDocument then hits line 1419-1422 with `bar: 2` left over and throws 'end of the stream or a document separator is expected'. readBlockSequence (line 992) breaks the same way for `﻿- a
- b`. The same mismatch also makes `hasSeparation = state.position === state.lineStart` (line 336) false, so a first-line `﻿# comment` is not skipped as a comment. It also blocks the separator checks guarded by `state.position === state.lineStart` (lines 776, 1388, 1402) on the first line, for example `﻿...`. The only BOM test, `load('﻿foo: bar
')` in test/core/units/load-other.test.mjs:7, has a single key, so it still passes.

findings.reason:
The diff removes skipByteOrderMark from the parseEvents loop (1454) and replaces testDocumentBoundary with bare testDocumentSeparator calls at 672, 776 and 1421. None of these skips a line-start U+FEFF. readDocument's '---' check at 1373 also sees the BOM, so in '---
a
﻿---

findings.claim: A BOM is now stripped only at offset 0. A BOM before a later document's '---' or '%' is no longer treated as a document boundary, so it becomes content or a parse error.
findings.evidence:
The diff removes `skipByteOrderMark(state)` from the `while (state.position < state.length)` loop in parseEvents. It also deletes `testDocumentBoundary`, which treated a line-start `﻿` followed by `---` or `%` as a document boundary. Its replacements at lines 672, 776 and 1421 call only `testDocumentSeparator`, which looks for `-`/`.` at the current position. Trigger: `loadAll('a
...
﻿--- b
')`. After the `...`, readDocument sees `﻿` rather than `---` at line 1373, so it sets no explicit start and parses `﻿--- b` as node content instead of starting a new document. In `foo
﻿---
bar`, readPlainScalar (line 776) no longer stops at the BOM-prefixed separator, and readDocument (line 1421) no longer accepts it as a boundary.

findings.reason: diff.patch touches only src/parser/parser.ts and adds no tests. A missing test is a coverage point, not a defect in itself, so I lowered it from medium to low. The defects it would have caught are the two items above.
findings.claim: No tests were added for the BOM and document-boundary paths that changed. The one existing BOM test uses a single-key input, which passes with both the old and new code.
findings.evidence: diff.patch touches only src/parser/parser.ts and adds no tests. The single unit test is `assert.deepStrictEqual(load('﻿foo: bar\n'), { foo: 'bar' })`, which is one key on one line. Nothing tests a BOM followed by a second line at column 0, a BOM followed by a comment, or a BOM before a later `---`/`%YAML` document. The yaml-test-suite fixtures that test/spec/spec.test.mjs would run (it maps `⇔` to `﻿`) are not in the export, so their coverage of these cases cannot be confirmed.
